subject: Food Science
title: Ultra-Processed Food Debate
description: A 60-second lesson on Ultra-Processed Food Debate.

hook.text: Ultra-processed food provides 60% of US calories. It's linked to obesity, cancer, and depression in study after study.

buildup.text: The NOVA classification defines ultra-processed food by its industrial ingredients—additives you'd never use at home.

discovery.text: A 2019 NIH trial proved it: people ate 500 more calories per day on ultra-processed diets versus whole food diets.

twist.text: Is it the additives causing harm—or the combination of sugar, fat, salt, and engineered palatability?

climax.text: Some scientists argue 'ultra-processed' is too vague. Fortified bread and infant formula are technically ultra-processed.

punchline.text: We know ultra-processed food harms. We still can't agree on why.

quiz.question: What did the 2019 NIH trial find about ultra-processed diets?
options: People ate 500 more calories per day versus whole food diets
